title: Watch movement on the bench
label: Watch movement in a knurled holder: perlage plate, four screwed clamps, striped barrel bridge with ratchet and crown wheels, Y train bridge over skeleton gears, pallet fork, balance under its cock, knurled crown.
caption: The balance sets the beat. Each swing tips the pallet fork, which lets the escape wheel advance half a tooth, so the mainspring's power leaves the barrel in eighths of a second. Drag across the figure to step through one beat at 1/20 speed.

tour.overview: A hand-wound movement: the crown winds the mainspring, the gear train carries its power, and the escapement and balance let it out one beat at a time.

steps.title: Winding
steps.text: Turning the crown turns the stem, the crown wheel and the ratchet wheel; the click drops into the ratchet's teeth so the wound spring cannot spin back.

steps.title: Mainspring barrel
steps.text: The mainspring is coiled inside the toothed barrel under its striped bridge. It is the watch's only store of power, enough for about two days.

steps.title: Gear train
steps.text: The barrel drives the centre, third and fourth wheels under the Y-shaped train bridge. Each pinion turns faster than the wheel before it, so the fourth wheel turns once a minute.

steps.title: Escapement
steps.text: The pallet fork locks the escape wheel with one of its two ruby stones. Each swing of the balance tips the fork, releasing the wheel by half a tooth and giving the balance a small push.

steps.title: Balance and hairspring
steps.text: The balance wheel swings back and forth on its hairspring, held under the cock, and its timing screws set the rate. It beats eight times a second, and that beat keeps the time.
